methode_en: Shoot every role as an identical locked-off shot (tripod, mid-chest, plain wall, 24 fps, locked exposure and focus), 10-15 s takes, clean voice peaking below -3 dBFS
Prepare one sheet per character (mouth closed, face unobstructed) and an empty background plate, with a shared style block
Body track for human or stylised roles: reference-driven video model (take = performance, sheet + background = reference images)
Body track for cartoon roles: motion control from an image of the character already placed in the set at the take's framing
Voice track in parallel: isolate the voice from the take, then convert it to a preset voice, never cloning a real person
Run a lip-sync pass only if the body track lost the lips
Conform each output to the take's size, frame rate and duration before any before/after comparison
controles_en: Compare face, preserved performance and mouth on key words for each method
Check size, fps and frame count match the take (outputs come back at 25/30 fps and truncated)
Respect the input limits read from the model schema (file < 10 MB, lip-sync audio ≤ 15 s)
pieges_en: Prompt reduced to "turn her into a knight": you must say the take only provides performance, framing and rhythm
Full profile or hands in front of the mouth: keep head turns within three-quarter view
The video-replacement track softens big movements and keeps the original wall

methode_en: Convert HDR (HLG) to SDR before any processing
Transcribe with word-level timestamps, cut false starts and pauses while snapping each cut to the real voice onset, then re-transcribe to prove no word is clipped
Extract a per-frame person matte, plus face and hand tracking
Write a beats file (which word triggers which effect): sub-pixel zooms hiding jump cuts, titles behind the head, word-by-word captions
Generate a sound-effects kit and sectioned music, then measure where the drop actually lands and align it with the key word
Optional, after a quote: a video-to-video pass that rebuilds the set while keeping face and lips, switched in on a chosen word
Mix: music ~18 dB under the voice before the drop, ~15 dB after, ducking, master at -14 LUFS, export H.264 BT.709 24 fps with motion blur
controles_en: Re-transcription of the cut matches the expected text word for word
Logo on screen for at least 2.5 s, never straddling a cut
Final loudness -14 LUFS; motion blur never crosses a cut
pieges_en: Whisper word endings are unreliable: follow the audio decay
Requested music section lengths are not respected: measure the drop
iPhone HDR video read as SDR: blown-out skin

methode_en: List every element in the shot: character, creature, prop, set
Characters and animals: legless capsule (with two or three distinctive marks) so the model invents a natural gait
Only rig a character if you have a clean cycle of the exact motion wanted
Props seen in the look image: a two-tone block is enough; products and set pieces approximated after image 1: generated 3D model
Send the video model the playblast (blocking, motion) + one finished image (look), with a prompt forcing it to follow the camera frame by frame
When in doubt, A/B test over a 4-8 s window, one parameterised scene per variant, same shared look image
controles_en: Contact sheet: clay row above the render row at six equal instants per variant
Counting clause in the prompt (the object changes hands exactly once)

pieges_en: Frozen legs: the character slides; sped-up walk cycle: stays a walk
Braziers as blocks: replaced by lanterns or gone
Copying then hand-editing a scene for the A/B: bias

methode_en: Draw the label flat (brand, flavour, one line), then a product sheet: front, left and right three-quarter, back, top
Create one still per step, each an edit of the previous one, approved before any video

Trim the same number of frames from the start of every output so they overlay
controles_en: Same resolution, frame count and frame rate for every step (e.g. 185 frames at 24 fps)

Measure landmarks on the mesh (crotch, base of neck, chin, half shoulder width) where clothing fools detection
Find the real wrists (glove edge by colour or material), place the joint ~1.5 cm towards the fingertips, refit the fingers
Move each joint to the same relative spot as on the mannequin, keeping bone orientations
Redo skin weights once, fix the knees, then check with a front and side overlay

Side-by-side comparison with the reference mannequin

methode_en: One change per request, stated precisely ("only the middle lantern in red")
Add a list of what must stay: face and identity, other objects, lighting, framing
For a pair of objects, explicitly name the one that stays
Keep the original aspect ratio; cost the plan (edits × models × attempts) before launching
Stacked edits: start from the previous step and repeat the full keep list, adding every edit already made
Compare two or three models when fidelity matters
controles_en: Difference map: only pixels in the requested area should light up
Original/result overlay: a doubled face signals a shift

methode_en: Generate a very wide, very large stand plate (telephoto, a dozen rows, no text)
For each fan: crop a 512 px square centred one face below the face to replace, edit only the person in the centre with a prop readable from afar, two variants
Realign the edit on the crop, match colours, paste it back through a mask of what changed
Run OCR on the final plate to erase any lettering on clothes and scarves
Redo each fan as a 16:9 TV close-up (~2K), neighbours blurred
Animate ~8 s with sound: indifferent, sees themselves on screen, reacts; "a single continuous take"
Cut to 16:9 and 9:16 and edit a reel with lower thirds in post

methode_en: Generate head, body, hand and props as separate 3D models, each from a plain-background image with no text
Assemble in Blender without silently moving approved parts
Rigged low-res rebuild: triangle budget (more on the face), details baked into PBR maps, humanoid skeleton with finger chains, T-pose, max 4 weights per vertex
Face: if the mouth is closed at rest, redo a head with parted lips, clean retopology, then 52 ARKit shapes with exact names including jaw, teeth, tongue
Motion: generated 5-10 s video, full body, plain background, static camera, converted to a skeleton then retargeted (time resampling, feet on the ground every frame)
Secondary motion: short bone chains for hair, damped spring on head rotation, clamped to a few degrees
controles_en: Count bones and shape keys in the file (e.g. 78 bones, 3 segments per finger, 52 shapes)
Textured and wireframe render of the same frame

Feet pointing toes-up after retargeting

methode_en: Gather 4 or 5 images, each showing a single idea on a neutral background

For each image, write what must not be borrowed from it ("pose only, don't show the mannequin")
Strict palette only if you name the allowed and banned inks; text quoted exactly with "no other words"
Generate the image (1536x1024), then look for leaks
Use the image as the first frame of a 6 s clip whose prompt describes only motion, camera and sound

Count the named elements in the final image

methode_en: Generate two images: empty green studio and the subject in its final pose in that studio, real floor with a taped grid
Animate between first and last frame to get the green-screen shot
Key the video with an alpha channel (try several tools on the same clip)
Composite the key over a generated background: at this stage it looks pasted on

Reuse the same green-screen shot to spin off several sets

Key present from the first frame, with no leaking tape line
Same instruction for every model compared, at most one sentence for a named flaw

Green visible through a visor or a window

methode_en: Story: a true behaviour as the payoff, 20 to 30 shots of 4-6 s, never two identical compositions in a row

Blender guides in saturated colours (each colour = one material or character), bumpy organic shapes, one camera per wide or crowded shot
Start frame: guide as reference 1, sheets after; end frame = an edit of the start frame
Animate between the two (4-6 s), sound off, then keep every other frame (12 unique frames/s at 24 fps)
Music cut to the edits, spot sound effects, master at -16 LUFS, -3 dB peak
controles_en: Frame-by-frame review: melting faces, extra legs, objects popping in
Counts checked on group shots (e.g. seven otters in the right order)
Final mix -16 LUFS, peak ≤ -3 dB, loudest section on the key moment

Identity mark too small (ear notch never rendered)
More than two characters per shot without a placement guide

Identical size and speed across directions

Write a look that adds a reactive world (dust, debris, birds) without new characters; mute the generated audio.
Render with one or two models and check each job's status and duration.
Measure the frame-by-frame offset between render and drawing, then retime or trim; prove alignment by overlaying only the extracted dark strokes.
controles_en: Mean offset measured on every render (the best model stayed under about 2.4 frames).
Padding card truly black: flat shading and emission at 0.
Output duration equal to the original frame count after retiming.
pieges_en: Judging timing by eye: a 198-frame shot fell up to 31 frames (1.3 s) behind, poses intact.
Stretching a shot whose world must move naturally: smoke and birds become too fast.
Overlaying the drawing in multiply mode: the grey background darkens everything.
exemples_en: Render my 2 s animatic in watercolour style without changing the timing.
Measure how many frames the render lags behind my drawing.
Compare Seedance and MiniMax on this shot.
grease-pencil-to-final-frame.illustration_en: Sliding wipe: left half blue pencil, right half painted render, same pose.

methode_en: Start from one reference image per fighter and turn it into a clean front sheet.
Convert the sheet to textured 3D (about 40,000 triangles).
Auto-rig onto a standard humanoid skeleton (52 bones).
For each move: animate a reference actor from a still into a short video, then convert the video to motion on the skeleton.
Assemble in three.js: game frames, hitboxes, flat-shaded rendering, sounds; multilingual voices and one music track per arena.
controles_en: Each video-to-motion clip reviewed on the character before integration (no published threshold).
Hitboxes tuned per move in game.
pieges_en: No skill shipped: method reconstructed from the page alone.
exemples_en: Create a rigged 3D fighter from my drawing.
Generate a spinning back kick for this character from a video.
Prepare ten basic moves for my game.
hibana.illustration_en: Flat-shaded fighter silhouette, five kick poses lined up like a move sheet.

methode_en: Casting: one full-length reference per person, front-facing, neutral grey outfit, margins of about 8%.
Clothing: one product photo with no visible mannequin per complete look, shoes included; sets generated separately.
Fit each person to each look as a "fitted master" and review it before any other step.
Build each editorial image from exactly three references (master, garment, set) with a precise asymmetric pose, not the catalogue pose.
From approved images only: a lateral walk (never towards the lens) and a loop that returns to the same frame; leave about 15% of floor below the shoes.
Pilot one person × one look × one set end to end before expanding the grid; one music track per set; estimate cost per video model.
controles_en: Review identity, garment construction, framing and exposure on every image.
Loop review: about 7 out of 55 rejected for changed closures or invented hems.
Cost comparison per film: budget model ≈ 100 credits vs ≈ 460 at 720p for the premium model (≈ 78% savings).
pieges_en: Try-on that opens a closed jacket or loses a metallic material: rerun with the original references.
Copying the master's stiff pose: the whole editorial must be redone.
Walk replaced by a pirouette; identical first and last frames don't guarantee a clean loop.
exemples_en: Put my three outfits on two models in four sets.
How much would the campaign cost in 1080p versus a cheaper model?
Add a 10 s lateral walk for each approved image.
impossible-fitting-room.illustration_en: 3×3 grid of thumbnails: same faces across rows, same outfits down columns, varied sets.

methode_en: Put the same style sentence in every concept prompt and always ask for dark navy-blue windows.
Separate moving parts by editing the approved concept (tower without sails, rotor alone) before 3D.
Convert each concept to textured 3D, preview from three angles, keep the originals.
Place each building in a lot slot that carries the spawn animation, so the model can be swapped.
Decimate: about 160,000 faces per building for the film, far fewer for the web.
For night: extract the navy blue from the textures by colour key and convert it to emission; switch the lighting.
controles_en: Every building has enough dark glazing to light up.
Boat heading compared with the concept (bow forward).
Shadows baked into textures spotted and cleaned.
pieges_en: Painting window masks by hand instead of using the colour key.
Windmill generated in one piece: sails welded to the tower.
Animating the model rather than the slot: a model swap loses the animation.
Raw image-to-3D output (about 1.9M triangles, 55 MB) shipped as is.
exemples_en: Generate six pastel houses in the same style for my island.
Make the windows light up when night falls.
Separate the windmill sails so they spin.
island-builder.illustration_en: Pastel island in two halves: left in broad daylight, right at night with golden windows.

methode_en: Generate a wide key image of the whole place in cutaway to set palette, light and mood.
Break the brief into rooms, machines, props, food, characters: one concept per object, same studio framing (light grey, 3/4 view, whole object); characters in front-facing A-pose.
Show the casting sheet and wait for a yes before any 3D.
Compare two to four image-to-3D models on one prop and one character, judging materials too; choose per object type.
Rig and share a walk cycle; action poses in code (reset each bone to rest, world-space targets); procedural architecture in headless Blender.
Paths on a grid computed from real collisions; compress models (geometry and WebP textures); about 120 s of music and a 30 s ambience loop.
controles_en: Seat and speech-bubble heights measured on each skeleton.
Point light count capped (cut from 18 to 9).
30 fps when nobody interacts, rendering stopped in a hidden tab; building compressed from 7.6 to 2.3 MB.
pieges_en: Absurd machinery for the real place: ask how the real place works.
Doing 3D before the casting is approved: nine meshes wasted.
Generated idle clip making the head jump: replace it with a pose in code.
Choosing a 3D model on shape alone: a black lacquered bowl turned grey.
exemples_en: Build a 3D cutaway of a bakery with three staff.
Show me the casting first before going to 3D.
Slim down the scene so it loads fast on the web.
kumo-ramen.illustration_en: Model of a food stall with its roof lifted, tiny cooks and customers, lanterns lit.

methode_en: Write the plan in frames (240 at 24 fps, EEVEE): opening image, props passing, light event, payoff.
Plan the camera after the light event so it frames it.
Generate signs, posters and menu with readable invented names, seamless PBR materials (wet floor), a 360 sky and two concept-to-3D hero props.
Decimate and apply heavy meshes (about 12% of the original).
Animate the sputtering sign with a constant-key power value (18 keys over about twenty frames).
Render test frames at key moments, fix, and continuously record a timestamped timelapse and build notes.
controles_en: Render time per frame: a 1.9M-face prop cost 8 to 17 s, brought down to 1-2 s after decimation.
Shadows only on the main lights; reflection probe off when the floor leaves the frame.
Open every test frame (rain under the awning, haze, saturated emissives, single hue).
No real logo in generated images.
pieges_en: Camera path drawn before the light event: the sign is never framed.
First frame dark and muddled even though it's the thumbnail.
Empty boxes where small signs hang.
exemples_en: Build a 10 s shot of a rainy alley with a sign that lights up.
Why does my render take 15 s per frame?
Generate a poster with a readable invented shop name.
last-order.illustration_en: Rainy alley at night, foreground puddle reflecting a neon sign flickering on.

methode_en: Write 4 to 6 acts on a single horizontal strip, one interaction per act and a final reveal.
Generate a hero image that serves as style reference for everything else.
Produce a kit of about 25 layers: opaque sky, wide repeating wave or ground strips, transparent cut-outs for every element.
Make each character as a parts sheet (fixed face, separate limbs) assembled and jointed in the page.
Scrolling drives camera and puppets; night is a tint applied to the same textures; interactions are buttons projected onto the cut-outs.
A single looping instrumental track, tail crossfaded into the head.
controles_en: Listen to and classify the music take before use (an early take was a nature ambience).
Music at about 10% so the effects can be heard.
Clickable areas active only once the curtains open; test every reachable camera.
pieges_en: Looping the raw file: the join is audible.
Horizon strip visible between two sea sheets when the camera rises.
exemples_en: Make a five-act children's story that reads as you scroll.
Cut my character into head, arms and legs to animate it.
Loop this music without an audible join.
little-paper-voyage.illustration_en: Small paper boat on three rows of cut-out waves, moon hanging on a string.

methode_en: Start from one finished reference render per design.
Ask an image model to extract each part (head, headless torso, arms, legs) onto its own sheet without redrawing it; name sides by position in the image and forbid mirroring.
Review the sheets, then convert each part to textured 3D.
Fit in code from geometry: fixed height per slot, feet facing forward, hip above ankle, shoulders aligned; only small per-part corrections.
Cut limbs into rigid pieces at knee, ankle and elbow so they bend without stretching the armour.
Redraw the support crew in A-pose with empty hands before animating; generate and measure music and effects.
controles_en: Left/right sides checked before image-to-3D.
Three designs = 18 parts mounted on the same attachment points.
Sound pitch and loudness measured (an alarm came back as a high beep).
pieges_en: Asking for a redesign instead of an extraction.
Torso keeping the head even though it's a separate part.
Automatic skinning on rigid armour: the plates stretch.
Animating a character whose tool is welded to the hand.
exemples_en: Split my robot into head, torso, arms and legs in 3D.
Mount robot A's legs on robot B's torso.
Make the knee bend without deforming the armour.
mech-bay.illustration_en: Hangar with three different mechs whose arms have been swapped, overhead crane above.

methode_en: Write each loop as a stateless drawing function of time, palette and size.
Pick each period so it divides 12 s exactly; draw randomness from an indexed deterministic function.
Check: the same instant rendered twice is identical, the 12 s frame equals the 0 s frame, no jump at the loop point compared with neighbouring motion.
Render 1920×1080 at 24 fps with sub-frame motion blur (8 by default, up to 40 for very fast motion), supersampling and H.264 BT.709 encoding.
Optional: place a keyed subject on the loop's clock, or overlay a keyed AI shot with ffmpeg.
controles_en: "Seam" failure if the 12 s frame differs from the 0 s frame.
"Non-deterministic" failure if the same instant gives two images.
Sample just before and after the loop point (11.9; 11.95; 0; 0.05 s).
pieges_en: Period that doesn't divide 12 s (5 s cycle): fix the period, never a crossfade.
Randomness or system date in the drawing.
3D projection divided by depth twice.
exemples_en: Make a 12 s animated background in my brand colours behind my title.
Put my keyed mascot on a waves loop.
Check this loop doesn't jump at the join.
motion-loops.illustration_en: Grid of nine colourful geometric thumbnails, each with a circular loop arrow.

methode_en: Keep the logo and one word identical, same position and same bounce; everything else changes on each landing.
Draw each world in SVG, CSS or canvas, rendered frame by frame (1080×1080 at 30 fps).
Speed up the bounce in steps (from 1.23 s to 0.7 s per bounce) every eight worlds.
Synthesise the music from the same timeline so every kick drum lands on a landing.
Add one sound effect per world, placed on its event frame.
Raster logo: vectorise it, then rebuild its layers by hand.
controles_en: Logo tilt proportional to sway speed, so it passes zero smoothly.
Font loaded before drawing a text mask.
Final run through a limiter set on the groove's peak; public-domain status checked for each tribute.
pieges_en: Leaving the rhythm to generated music: it doesn't follow tempo changes.
SVG nested inside an SVG: the logo disappears.
Believing a vectorised logo keeps its layers.
exemples_en: Make my logo bounce through ten different styles over 30 s.
Sync a beat to every bounce.
Add a different sound for each world.
one-logo-42-worlds.illustration_en: The same logo in four panels: green terminal, swirling starry sky, op art, neon.

methode_en: Set up a camera study in Blender: stand-in silhouettes, source camera, new cameras; check headroom and blocked views on a contact sheet.
Generate the master image, then a second pass that widens the frame and restores full silhouettes.
Shoot the continuous source take (low-res pilots first).
Write the recut: continuity contract (same person, props, eyelines, time base), actions as observed in the take, numbered shot list with times and focal lengths.
Generate the recut in one go with the take as reference video.
Measure the actual cut points and exact duration on the result, then edit and compare source and recut side by side.
controles_en: Cuts measured, never taken from the prompt (a cut requested at 1.35 s lands around 1.9-2.2 s; the last one requested at 18.2 s lands around 19.4-19.8 s).
Duration read with ffprobe, not from the last contact-sheet sample.
Same final hold added to both films.
pieges_en: Writing the recut from the planned choreography rather than from what the take shows.
Taking an LLM's reading of contact sheets as timing truth.
Stopping at the first master: a recut can only cut into what the source contains.
exemples_en: Turn this single shot into a sequence of ten different angles.
Where do the cuts really fall in this render?
Prepare a camera study in Blender before generating.
one-take-many-angles.illustration_en: Top view of a character surrounded by thirteen small numbered cameras and their focal lengths.

methode_en: Build at true miniature scale and shoot with real depth of field, not a post-production blur.
Generate flat, orthographic, full-page facades, with sign text quoted exactly.
Generate PBR papers, concept-to-3D hero props, room backdrop and environment lighting.
Animate with Blender Python (banded waves, boat, camera); place each sound on its second and ask for music slightly longer than the picture.
Have renders reviewed by image analysis; turn each remark into a measured change; keep v1 next to v2.
controles_en: Hull checked frame by frame: in v1 the waves hid it on 290 of 360 frames.
Bounds printed for each placement (a lighthouse was floating 14 cm up).
Music scanned for silence gaps (1.4 s to 4.8 s in one take).
pieges_en: Faking tilt-shift with a blur gradient.
Facades generated in perspective or with sky and ground.
Believing the HDR step produced HDR when it produced 8-bit previews.
Rebuilding the scene to record the timelapse.
exemples_en: Make a short 15 s film of a paper village at sunrise.
Review this render and tell me what's wrong.
Place a seagull cry at 5.4 s and a bell at 10 s.
paper-harbor.illustration_en: Paper sailboat leaving a quay of folded houses, striped lighthouse, sun on a stick.

methode_en: Define the building in numbers (plinth, grid, columns, roof module, glazing) and model it with metre-based UVs that follow each element.
Plan one shot per lighting state, cut on markers; check that light can reach what the camera looks at.
Generate a first sky, then the other hours with that sky as reference, convert to environment lighting; save a "look" per state (world, suns, emissives, exposure).
Generate tileable materials, invented posters and signage (legibility checked by caption), concept-to-3D furniture and trees.
Capture visitors from a video performance onto their rig; add music and sounds.
Review with a quality score and a strict art review; a second pass changes only what was flagged.
controles_en: Test frames under the real render load (a shared GPU can triple the time).
Keep and report the harsher score of the two reviews.
Dusk render brought down from about 190 s to 5 s per frame.
pieges_en: Black glass with a Fresnel gradient that reads as blue plastic.
Low sun under a deep roof with no opening: black interior.
Rebuilding the scene to redo the timelapse.
exemples_en: Make a 30 s film of my house from noon to dusk.
Generate the golden-hour and night skies from this one.
Add a visitor who walks in and looks at a painting.
pavilion.illustration_en: Pavilion with a timber lattice roof by a lake, three sky bands: noon, gold, night blue.

methode_en: Start from a recording or screenshots of the game, logo, store links and genre; use the supplied art as is and only generate missing pieces in its style.
Build a single HTML file with no network requests, with a verb understood within 2 s.
The game waits for the first touch, a pulsing target, a hand showing the right gesture; it never plays for the player.
Three endings: goal reached, 35-45 s cap, 10 s of inactivity; an honest sentence of 1.5 s at most, then the end card.
Package for each ad network (MRAID, Meta, Google, AppLovin, Unity, Mintegral, Moloco, Liftoff, Pangle).
Test in a headless browser: base checks plus per-network checks, then each network's official preview.
controles_en: 19 base checks plus per-network checks (67 of 67 on the template).
Progress stays at 0 before the first touch; the mute button never counts as the first touch.
The hand returns after 2.5 s of inactivity and only shows.
State which network tools were actually passed.
pieges_en: Any form of autoplay or automatic move.
Game targets under the mute button.
Store screenshots taken as game art without approval.
exemples_en: Make a playable ad for my puzzle from this gameplay video.
Package it for AppLovin and Unity Ads.
Check it never plays on its own.
playable-ads.illustration_en: Vertical phone showing a sorting puzzle, dotted hint hand and mute button at bottom left.

methode_en: Lock the vehicle, equipment categories, screen sizes, visual direction and budget.
Generate a concept, then rebuild it as named parts, stored in an editable Blender kit.
Compose finishes of three coordinated materials: generated colour, roughness and metal calibrated locally.
Generate several panoramic worlds and workshop music.
Build the web configurator (orbit, exploded view, part mixing) with PNG, GLB and .blend export.
Keep a provenance record: prompts, parameters, rejected candidates and reasons, generated vs retouched content kept separate.
controles_en: Real walkthrough in the browser with captures; exported files reopened.
30 fps cap active, no continuous work at idle, click targets checked.
Technical audio validation kept separate from listening.
pieges_en: Rerunning old rebuild scripts that restore outdated geometry.
Publishing temporary signed URLs in the record.
Believing a successful local build proves the deployment.
exemples_en: Make a configurator for my buggy with three wheel options.
Suggest three coordinated finishes: ceramic, copper, carbon.
Export my configuration as GLB and .blend.
rover-foundry.illustration_en: Lunar rover in exploded view, wheels and antenna pulled apart, three material swatches beside it.

methode_en: Approve one master photo per product (shape, framing, light; 3/4 view if temples must show) and write its identity list and variable axes.
Choose per product: full chained edits when the material changes global shading (bag: leather, then flap, then clasp, each step from an approved image), otherwise masked edits as layers.
For layers: masks fitted to the part alone (metal only, up to the hinge, to the setting's outline), keep only changed pixels, in aligned layers.
Flatten each combination (6 eyewear edits give 27 combinations).
Generate each on-model try-on in a single pass; cut the colour swatches from the photos.
Name precisely any flaw to remove and redo the variations from the cleaned image.
controles_en: Every image passes the master's identity list; when flipping through, only the chosen part changes.
No fringe of the old material at a part's edge; stones fill their setting.
Likeness and lens tint stable across all try-on combinations; no generated text or logo.
pieges_en: Cut layers for a leather change: the whole bag's shading changes.
Full-frame mask to change a metal: the model redraws the frame.
Relighting a finished try-on: the glasses distort.
Building on an output that has drifted.
exemples_en: Make this bag in four leathers and three clasps.
Change only the lens colour, keep the frame.
Show each pair of glasses worn by two models.
same-product-every-variation.illustration_en: The same bag photographed nine times in a grid, only the leather and flap colour varying.

methode_en: Take the photo or scan of the user's sketch; a few strokes for the main masses are enough.
Render in colour with the sketch as reference; the prompt only adds style, colours and materials.
Generate once per theme a blank card frame whose window is a perfectly flat #00FF00 green.
Read height, normal, roughness and metal maps from the frame and the back; build the metal mask from colour.
Key out the character, set it in slight relief in front of a background, engrave the name on the measured plate, composite the user's logo on the back locally.
Convert the same render to textured 3D and slim it down (about 110,000 to 150,000 triangles, 1K WebP textures, 1 to 3 MB).
controles_en: Green window checked free of gradient or texture before reading any maps.
Metal mask taken from hues, not from the metal map (mother-of-pearl read as metal at 214/255).
Logo position measured on the real plate, not a fixed box.
pieges_en: Reference-image calls launched in parallel: refusals in bursts; send them one at a time.
Asking the model to reproduce a trademarked logo: refused; composite it locally.
Frame generated with the art already in place: green fringe around the character.
exemples_en: Turn my dragon drawing into a shiny game card.
Also make a 3D figurine of the same character.
Create a reusable black-and-gold card frame for my whole series.
sketch-to-asset.illustration_en: Pencil sketch of a little wizard on the left, his tilted gold card in the centre, his 3D figurine on the right.

methode_en: Write a one-page brief: rules, HUD, beat sheet (hook, loop, reward, end card).
Generate a style anchor sheet (pieces, UI, hero) passed as reference to every later image.
Generate transparent asset sheets and cut them into sprites (alpha islands or grid), named in order and checked on a contact sheet.
Code the gameplay as a deterministic program (rules engine, event list, renderer) that draws these sprites.
Reserve AI video for painted shots and hero moments, animated between painted first and last frames so they join; Blender optional for layouts, dice and crowds.
Two checkpoints: plan (6 to 10 key images and a low-res animatic with scratch voice), then a low-res edit with 100% crops before the final render.
controles_en: At 1920×1080: 64 px margins, body text ≥ 24 px, labels ≥ 20 px, nothing overflowing or overlapping.
Credits taken from a reconciled log, one per job, failures checked for refunds.
Two takes compared on the same input when two models are close.
pieges_en: Letting the video model play: illegal moves, jumping counters, health bars going back up.
Clips that look sped up.
Casting too close to a famous game.
exemples_en: Make a 30 s ad for my match-3 with a real board that follows the rules.
Cut this pieces sheet into named sprites.
Show me the animatic before launching the final render.
tap-to-install.illustration_en: Vertical match-3 board with crisp pieces, a single painted hero piece bursting into light.

methode_en: Split the roles: grey playblast = camera, focal length, framing, timing and motion; finished image per cut = style and light; sheets = identity; text = story states.
Build the blockout in Blender and place generated 3D models for set, ground and sky.
Generate reference sheets for recurring characters, props and locations.
Produce a look image, then a finished image per cut, aligned with the playblast.
Generate each shot in reference mode with the playblast as motion video; everything that must move must move in the playblast.
Narration, music and effects synced to picture; a single edit list rebuilt from each cut's latest valid take.
controles_en: Before sending: playblast, look image and finished image overlaid at 50%, positions matching.
After: take/playblast overlay on first, middle and last frame; search for hard cuts and dissolves.
Legs alternating, feet planted, motion in the right direction; same face, costume, two hands, whole prop.
Review video of film over playblast with cut number and timecode; an eyeball pass always added.
pieges_en: Conflicting inputs: the model settles it by cutting, dissolving or inventing.
Fixing by prompt alone: rarely stable from cut to cut; fix upstream.
Overwriting a take instead of versioning.
exemples_en: Keep my 30 cuts consistent from my Blender playblast.
Make me the review video with cut numbers.
The lantern switches hands in cut 12: find the cause.
the-last-lantern.illustration_en: Left half of the frame in grey blockout, right half a painted forest, a traveller and her lantern in the centre.

methode_en: Put the car image as first reference in every prompt and restate its key features in words.
Performer: supplied photo or a few castings on a sheet; lock a final look.
Generate the music in sections (intro with isolated hits, build, drop, break, return, finale), then measure the real tempo and accents.
Write each start image like a camera report and get images approved before animating (video ≈ 10 times the price of an image).
Animate each shot (1080p, about 5 s, one camera move, one action, motion from the first frame).
Cut on measured accents, normalise to -14 LUFS, optionally add graphics in code; end on a first/last-frame shot into a white studio and the 3D model.
controles_en: Same car and same performer in every shot.
Every cut on a measured accent; no clip starting frozen; no flaw at the out point.
Costs per ad taken from the jobs (final clips and images only).
pieges_en: Cutting on a fitted tempo grid: drift after a half-time drop.
Trusting the requested tempo (150 BPM requested, 120 obtained).
Two very short shots just before an impact; near-identical consecutive angles.
Graphics presenting the ad as an AI generation.
exemples_en: Make a 40 s ad for my car with a dancer, cut to the beat.
Measure the accents in this music and place the cuts.
End on the car spinning in a white studio.
the-showroom.illustration_en: Red car in profile, music waveform below with vertical marks at the cut points.

methode_en: Open a session log: start time, then one line per job (model, prompt, inputs, outputs, ID, end time, cost, kept or not).
Plan a single camera move with one key image per stage and a change every 4 to 6 s.
Turn a drawing into a separate body and clothes, convert each to 3D, rig, then dress and animate the first steps.
Render each key image in Blender, then finish it with an image model keeping the render as reference.
Reveal the world in render blocks composited from Blender.
Finish the full playblast in one video pass with the key images as look references; display the clock computed from the log.
controles_en: Each clock value = end time of the job closing the stage minus session start, never from memory.
Every compositing stage inspected on a rendered sheet.
No readable text invented by the video model; character mask locked to the tiles.
pieges_en: Naming a camera move in the video prompt: the model invents another one; describe the first frame's framing instead.
Shaded playblast colours surviving the video finish.
Rain as thick bars, flat sky, empty street, centred framing.
exemples_en: Make a shot showing my character built from sketch to walking.
Display the real time of each stage from the log.
Finish this Blender render in an illustrated style without changing the framing.
twenty-minutes.illustration_en: Character half grey mesh, half dressed, digital clock in the corner.

methode_en: Generate a seamless top-down pixel art ground texture, palette chosen per terrain, small motifs spread out; describe what is present, with no negations.
For each direction, find two motif-free areas that become the edge strips (two colours per edge).
Give each of the 16 tiles a centre taken from elsewhere in the texture, most with their own motif.
Join strips and centres with a minimum-error cut, no blending, to stay true pixel art.
Mask objects too large for a tile (over ~80% of its size, dilated by 2 px) so no sample touches them.
Export for Tiled, Godot, Unity and the web, and render a loop video comparing a repeated tile with the Wang set.
controles_en: Check each generation actually returned an image (over half the runs came back empty while still billed).
Real motif size measured (requested at 3-6 px, rendered at 8-20 px).
Reference repeated tile chosen with average detail, for a fair comparison.
pieges_en: Negations in the prompt: excluded objects appear.
Highly structured materials (water, bricks, planks) as an edge set: visible diamonds; use a corner set.
Keeping only the barest centres: the Wang side looks empty.
exemples_en: Make me a pixel art desert floor that doesn't show the grid.
Export the tileset for Godot.
Why do my water tiles make diamonds?
wang-tiles.illustration_en: Snow map split in two: the same pebble in rows on the left, natural grid-free ground on the right.
